prospects.thesis: AMD is executing on its MI350/MI400 accelerator roadmap and taking meaningful share in AI datacenter GPUs as hyperscalers diversify away from single-vendor dependence. With bullish options flow, bullish institutional positioning, and a +30% monthly move confirming momentum, the setup reflects growing conviction that AMD is the credible #2 in AI silicon. The $991B cap approaching the trillion-dollar threshold could act as a psychological catalyst into year-end.

ARM's royalty model is a pure-play beneficiary of both AI datacenter (Neoverse/Grace) and edge-AI proliferation across smartphones and automotive, with v9 adoption driving royalty rates materially higher. Bullish options and institutional flows plus +18.5% monthly momentum reflect market recognition of the licensing inflection. The 58.7x P/S is rich but justified by the highest-margin, capital-light business model in semis.

SMCI is the leading AI server integrator with liquid-cooled rack-scale solutions for Blackwell and MI350 deployments, and at 0.7x P/S it trades at a striking discount versus the rest of the AI complex following prior accounting overhangs. Bullish options and institutional signals plus +12.9% monthly performance suggest the rehabilitation story is gaining traction. Near-term catalyst: hyperscaler capex re-acceleration into calendar Q4.

SAIC provides mission-critical IT modernization, AI-enabled analytics, and space/C4ISR systems to DoD and intelligence customers, positioning it at the intersection of defense tech and AI adoption. At 0.7x P/S with bullish institutional flow, it offers defensive characteristics valuable against a backdrop of a rising 10Y yield (5.24%) and expanding VIX. FY26 backlog conversion and space-segment wins are near-term catalysts.

CACI is a leader in signals intelligence, electronic warfare, and defense software — categories receiving priority funding in the FY27 defense budget cycle. Bullish options flow contrasts with bearish institutional read, creating a divergence worth monitoring; the slight monthly pullback (-1.6%) offers a more attractive entry than chasing extended defense names. Catalyst: pending SIGINT/EW contract awards and continued Ukraine/Israel replenishment demand.
